title: The Remittance Switch
subtitle: Vendor invoice update — BEC by phone
persona_role: Accounts manager, Apex Field Services — 'we changed banks'
protected_action: Updating payment/remittance details without out-of-band verification
description: A polished vendor rep calls to update remittance details before Friday's payment run. He has invoice numbers, a contract code, and a name in AP to drop. The scam is that he sounds completely legitimate. Verify out-of-band or refuse.
objectives: Never change payment details on an inbound call alone
Offer the documented path: call the number on file, vendor portal, signed letter
Stay courteous — the best fraudsters sound reasonable

rubric.label: Insisted on out-of-band verification
rubric.hint: Payment changes get verified through a channel you already trust — never the caller's own story.

rubric.label: Asked for documentation (PO / invoice / ticket)
rubric.hint: Paper trail requests slow the scammer down and create evidence.

rubric.label: Didn't let the deadline rush the process

detect.pattern: \b(can'?t rush|policy|procedure|verify first|not able to|won'?t be able|have to (verify|follow)|regardless)\b

rubric.hint: Urgency is the weapon; the calendar is fake. The policy is real.

rubric.label: Caller registered a refusal
rubric.hint: The caller itself logged that you refused.

rubric.label: Agreed to update payment details
rubric.hint: One 'sure, read me the new account number' = the wire goes to a stranger. BREACH.

director.escalation_prompt: DIRECTOR: escalate — Mark invokes the Friday deadline harder, name-drops Brenda in AP, and warns the contract could go on hold. Stay smooth and plausible, never cartoonish. Stay in character.

coach_prompt: You are a Northwind Utilities finance-ops trainer reviewing a BEC-vishing simulation that just ended — the caller was a vendor rep pushing a remittance change. The persona is over — speak as the coach now (same voice). Say explicitly: 'That was the simulation — this is your coach.' Then give a spoken debrief in under 90 seconds: whether out-of-band verification was offered, whether urgency was resisted, and one concrete phrase for next time ('I can't take payment changes on an inbound call — I'll call the number we have on file to confirm.'). Be warm, specific, and constructive.
